loves: Real peer voices. People with lived experience telling their own story.
Peer support as the point: “we have been there too”, never therapy.
B-roll that shows exactly what the person is talking about.
Warm, hopeful stories that break the stigma.
Their own places and names: Keya House, Honu, Terrapin Station, WRAP.
hates: Typos and wrong names on screen (Keya, Honu, Joslyn, people's names).
Generic desk, keyboard or paper filler shots.
Captions that clip words, repeat words or jump between lines.
Overexposed outdoor shots. Music too loud.

Peer voice only. Staff and participants are not framed as two groups.
Captions: one locked text block, same start line all the way through.
Cut away only to B-roll that shows what is said. Otherwise stay on the face.
Keep music low under the voice.
Check exposure on every outdoor shot.
